description: The Water Data Exchange (WaDE) is the Western States Water Council programme that pulled water rights, water supply and water use data from many western US state agencies into one shared structure, with WestDAAT as the search and download front end. The programme page says WaDE and WestDAAT remain publicly available in a static, read-only form, that the last data updates were completed in March 2026, and that the council does not plan to update or curate them further. It advises users to treat the exchange as a historical, multi-state reference and to go first to each state agency's official portal, which stay the authoritative source for state-administered rights and use. The page also links data documentation, use cases and a list of state water data portals. Coverage: western member states of the council, with the content and definitions of each state's own systems carried through. Access: free; the licence is not stated on the page read. Caveats: frozen since early 2026, state definitions differ, and the page does not give record counts. It supports cross-state analysis of water allocation, priority dates and demand for irrigation and municipal supply, including drought curtailment scenarios, and relates to the USGS water use records in the catalogue while pointing to state portals for current data.
